title: Modernize tracing hooks and add log->metric harvester to reduce hotpath allocations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Runtime traces and logs are contributing significant CPU and allocation overhead in the inference hotpath. Current tracing hooks allocate per-request context objects and build high-cardinality spans for optional fields, and logs are emitted for events that would be more cost-effective as metrics. Goal: reduce tail CPU/allocations and metric emission cost by modernizing tracing hooks to a pooled, zero-alloc hotpath and introducing a small, service-side log->metric harvester that converts selected log events into structured metrics before export.
acceptance_criteria: P95 CPU on serving runtime reduced by at least 12% for observability-related work under 95th percentile load compared to baseline
Median allocations per request attributable to tracing code reduced by >= 60% in microbenchmarks
Span cardinality for request-level traces bounded to configured keys; dynamic tags default to sampling-disabled unless opt-in
Log->metric harvester produces stable schematized metrics with <1% additional latency and reduces exported log volume for selected events by >= 70%
No functional regressions in trace propagation across async/gRPC boundaries (validated by integration tests and end-to-end trace roundtrip tests)
implementation_notes: Introduce a SpanPool with fixed-size ring buffer for short-lived span objects; spans taken from pool on hotpath and returned after end
Refactor existing tracing hooks to accept pre-allocated span context and to avoid map[string]interface{} allocations for common fields
Introduce an opt-in per-route "dynamic_tags" whitelist to prevent high-cardinality user metadata from becoming span keys by default

Implement a lightweight log2metric harvester as an in-process filter: pattern-matching on log event name + stable schema -> increment counters/histograms; emits metrics to our metrics sink rather than full log payload
Add feature flags and gradual rollout toggles: span-pool, compact-span-proto, and log2metric-harvester so we can rollback quickly
Create unit and integration tests: allocation regressions, span propagation matrix (sync/async/gRPC/http), and e2e pipeline validation with dev telemetry cluster
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Span pooling could leak if not returned on panic paths. Mitigation: ensure defer-return wrappers and addressable guard rails; add fuzz tests for panics and goroutine leaks

Risk: log->metric mapping may lose important debug context. Mitigation: retain full logs for a short window and route reduced sampling of full logs to long-term storage; add dashboards to monitor dropped context

Risk: Changing span shape may break downstream consumers and dashboards. Mitigation: maintain compatibility layer (compact-span-proto) that preserves API for consumers and run in parallel for one release cycle

Risk: Unforeseen performance regression in rare customer workflows. Mitigation: enable canary rollout to 5% of traffic and advanced tracing if regressions detected, automatically rollback via rollout policy
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): implement span pool + refactor hooks behind FEATURE_SPAN_POOL flag and run microbenchmarks (unit + perf harness)
Phase 2 (staging): deploy compact-span-proto and log2metric harvester behind flags to staging clusters; run latency/cpu/alloc A/B for 48 hours
Phase 3 (canary): enable for 5% traffic in a single region; monitor P50/P95 CPU, allocs, and span integrity; keep full logs forwarded for 24h
Phase 4 (ramp): 25% -> 75% -> 100% with automated checks and rollback thresholds defined in rollout policy
Phase 5 (post-release): deprecate old tracing path after one release if no issues; publish migration notes for downstream consumers
notes: Spike earlier showed ~18% allocation reduction in microbenchmarks when moving from map tags to preallocated arrays
